title: Ripple Counter: How Four Toggle Flip-Flops Count to Sixteen
topic: 4-bit asynchronous ripple counter — chain four toggle (T = J = K = 1) flip-flops with each Q driving the next stage's clock. Each stage halves the frequency, so Q_0 is the least significant bit toggling every clock, Q_3 is the most significant bit toggling every eight clocks; together they count 0000 → 1111. The 'ripple' name comes from the propagation delay cascade: bits flip one stage at a time, not simultaneously.

beats.narration: Chain four toggle flip-flops together — what do they count to?

elements.content: Four toggling cells, one clock — a binary counter falls out.

beats.narration: Wire four toggle flip-flops in a chain — the clock drives only the first one, and each Q output drives the clock of the next stage.

elements.content: Four T flip-flop boxes in a horizontal row, labeled FF0..FF3
Each box: J=K=1 fixed inputs (toggle mode); CLK input on left, Q output on right
CLK input wire feeds FF0; Q_0 wire connects to FF1.CLK; Q_1 → FF2.CLK; Q_2 → FF3.CLK
Output labels Q0..Q3 (LSB to MSB) above each Q wire
asynchronous — each stage clocks the next one

beats.narration: Run the clock. The first stage toggles every edge, the second one every two edges, the third one every four, and the fourth one every eight — the four Q outputs together spell out a binary count from zero up to fifteen.

elements.content: Four-bit register display Q3 Q2 Q1 Q0 with each bit lighting amber when high
Decimal readout below the binary register (0..15)
Clock pulse counter ticking once per period; each rising edge advances the count by one
the least-significant bit flips every clock; the next one every other clock; …

beats.narration: Stack the four Q outputs and the divide-by-two structure jumps out — each row is a clean square wave at half the frequency of the row above.

elements.content: Five stacked timing rows: CLK (top, fastest), then Q0, Q1, Q2, Q3 — each at half the frequency of the previous
Row labels CLK, Q0, Q1, Q2, Q3 on the left
Period annotations: T, 2T, 4T, 8T, 16T from CLK down to Q3
N stages → divide-by-2^N — and the bit pattern itself counts

beats.narration: N flip-flops give an N bit counter that rolls over every two to the N clocks — small, simple, fast.

elements.content: asynchronous = simple; ripple delay grows with N. For wide, fast counters, prefer a synchronous design.
the building block of every timer, frequency divider, and event counter
